scope:
Audit E-P7 placement and original load -> image-initialized private state.

The boot prefix is an explicit resident input. Only lower storage transfers are
modeled; code banks begin as poison and are not supplied as resident firmware.
No new CPU model, firmware build, package output, SHA or camera operation.
remaining_conditions: The entire boot prefix remains original. It is resident input here; physical reset is not emulated.
The two code-bank interiors have finite reference and load evidence, not exhaustive ownership or physical execute/cache qualification.
CPU2 pool capacity and prefix instructions remain original; no private pool reservation or cold-clear hook remains.
Known copy/clear/arena intervals do not collide. This does not exclude unknown or indirect later writes, resets or DMA.
Lower storage success and coherent cached/uncached aliases are explicit models; the earlier failing-read evidence is unchanged.
Whole task/IRQ stack bounds, physical startup/display/photo behavior and independent recovery remain unproved.

candidate_build_report.scope: Build a NON-INSTALLABLE E-P7 build1100 decoded candidate; no updater container or hashes.
limits: Both executable regions are unqualified placement assumptions, not proven free space.
Private state occupies an image-initialized loaded tail with one uncached access alias; all-writer ownership remains unproved.
The boot prefix and all CPU2 pool slots remain original; no new prefix loader or pool reservation is required.
Early copy failure, secondary CPU ordering and cache visibility remain unresolved.
Full capture/alias retirement, queue/task lifetime, cancellation and GUI exclusion remain unresolved.
Complete task/IRQ stack bounds remain unknown; .su data are local function measurements only.
H/L persistence is excluded; this is the existing volatile implementation.
No updater acceptance, recovery, camera execution, image-quality or display acceptance is established.

private_storage.method: fishcu loaded-section initialized state; E-P7-specific placement
